title: CP2463-23 Devon & Torbay Local Electric Vehicle Infrastructure
description:
Concession contract for:\r
\r
The Councils intend to work with Private Sector Partner(s) (PSP) using a concessions approach, supplemented with the LEVI Capital Funding, to deliver approximately 2000 electric vehicle chargepoints in car parks and on-street locations across Devon & Torbay.\r
\r
This is a joint project between Devon County Council and Torbay Council. The Devon District authorities (East Devon District Council, Exeter City Council, Mid Devon District Council, Teignbridge District Council, South Hams District Council, Torridge District Council, and West Devon Borough Council) and Devon Parish Councils are also delivery partners contributing to the successful delivery of the project, which will include granting leases at council owned car parks.\r
\r
The Lots for this procurement are split based on the type of chargepoint, as per the Specification. \r
\r
Lot 1 is for Rapids DC (50kW+)\r
Lot 2 is for Fast AC (22kW)\r
Lot 3 is for Standard AC (<8kW) Bollard Chargepoints\r
Lot 4 is for On-Street Lamp Column Chargepoints \r
\r
Although at the outset Torbay Council will not be awarded under every Lot, the Authority reserves the right to modify the contract to allow Torbay Council to call off at a later date by mutual agreement with the successful provider.

title: CP2564-24 County Farms Opportunities Research
description:
The County Farms Estate (CFE) are interested in commissioning a piece of research to explore how to improve economic and environmental resilience within the CFE, and how to maximise future opportunities brought about by changes in the food and farming sector. It is expected that this could include the adoption of regenerative and innovative practices; use of agri-tech; sharing knowledge and examples of best practice; diversification, including into horticulture; and alternative routes to market.

The research will build on previous learning developed by the DCC Economy Enterprise and Skills team through the Future Farming Resilience Programme; the Devon Agri-Tech Alliance; the Devon Farm Innovation Toolkit and Carbon toolkit; and the Agri Innovation Pilot currently being undertaken in West Devon and South Hams and expanded separately by the Satellite Catapult Environmental Space Living Lab (ESLL) Project. The research will also take into account other drivers from within DCC, including objectives set by the Growth Strategy and potential Devolution Deal; the Devon Carbon Plan; the Devon Food Partnership; and the Local Nature Recovery Strategy.

This proposed research will run in parallel with an extended agri-innovation business support pilot for CFE tenants.

The scope of the study should identify opportunities and challenges for the CFE in terms of relevant land and livestock management processes and methodologies, which can be adopted in order to: increase resilience to climate change and other challenges; improve profitability and productivity; and demonstrate models of best practice through the CFE in terms of wider DCC policy and strategy. To include: Review of the baseline data for the CFE and its tenants; review of previous research and learning in the context of the CFE (including but not limited to the below) and identification of any gaps; review of national, regional and local policy and strategy in the context of the CFE (including but not limited to the below) and an exploration of challenges and opportunities; exploration of the unique challenges and opportunities for the CFE and what support tenants might need to build resilience and take up opportunities; exploration of how the CFE and other DCC pilots and programmes can work together to demonstrate and support best practice - in the context of local strategy and policy - within the CFE and the wider Devon farming community. 

The Contract has a set budget of £40,000.00

title: CP2300-22 - Contract for the Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste
description:
Devon County Councils current contract arrangements for the transportation and treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste collected by the eight district councils within Devon is due to expire at the end of March 2024 and as such DCC are seeking to reprocure this service.  It is intended that the new contract will operate from 1st April 2024 for an initial period of five years with the option to extend the contract by a period or periods totalling a maximum further 5 years.\r
\r
Organic Sweepings Waste mainly consists of organic matter and as such DCC wishes the waste to be treated to allow it to be recycled e.g. into a compost like product or similar.\r
\r
The service requirement has been divided into two lots and DCC intends to let a contract for each lot.   Bidders can submit bids for one or both lots with no limit on the number of lots to be awarded to one provider.  Bids for each lot must be independent and not reliant on being awarded both lots.\r
\r
The Lots are as follows\r
\r
Service Lot 1 Contract for the transportation and Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste from the District Councils of \r
East Devon\r
Exeter\r
Mid Devon\r
North Devon\r
South Hams\r
Torridge\r
West Devon\r
\r
Organic Sweepings waste arising from the District Councils covered in Lot 1 will require transportation from Waste Collection Points provided by DCC or District Council to the Contractors Waste Treatment Point for Treatment.\r
\r
During the 2022 23 Financial Year approximately 3600 tonnes of Organic Sweepings were collected as part of the District Councils covered by Lot 1 sweeping operations. \r
\r
Service Lot 2 Contract for the transportation and Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste from Teignbridge District Council.\r
\r
The Contractor is required provide their own Waste Reception Point within the administrative boundary of Teignbridge District Council to which Organic Sweepings Waste can be delivered by Teignbridge District Council.   After Teignbridge District Council has delivered their Organic Sweepings Waste to the Contractors Waste Reception Point the Contractor shall transport the waste to the Contractors Waste Treatment Point for Treatment.\r
\r
During the 2022 23 Financial Year Teignbridge District Council collected approximately 950 tonnes of Organic Sweepings as part of their sweeping operations.\r
\r

title: CP2354-23 SPF Agri Innovation Programme
description:
Devon County Council have designed an intensive Agri Innovation programme tailored to the demand in West Devon and South Hams.\r
\r
The overall aim of the project is to support farm businesses in West Devon and South Hams to maximise their potential and productivity through regenerative and innovative methods and practices. This will be for 20 farms per Lot providing 30 hours of support per farm.\r
\r
The primary objective is to undertake a thorough farm innovation diagnostic carbon audit and business plan will be undertaken with support from an agri advisor. This will be followed by identification of further support needed to implement farmers plans. Where possible this will be facilitated through the programme and could include but not limited to testing of soils and water and carbon deep dives and grant searches and guided support to access grant funding opportunities. In addition beneficiaries will have access to enhanced knowledge sharing and collaborative opportunities through the Devon Agri Tech Alliance and wider stakeholder networks.

description:
To prepare a Masterplan option study for site PLY7 (Colin Campbell Court) allocated in the Plymouth and South West Devon Joint Local Plan (JLP) and adjoining land (Frankfort Gate South). A Second Part of the Commission seeks to extend the brief to the north of Frankfort Gate, forming the land bounded by Western Approach to the west and Cornwall Street as far as the Market Way. The extent of the wider masterplan and the two distinct areas north and south of Frankfort Gate are shown on the plan below. The team should be led by a Master Planner / Urban Design Consultant, but include transport engineers, property consultants, cost consultancy and local real estate agency advice.\r
It is our ambition for an exciting and dynamic mixed use, residential led new quarter for the city building upon the best in sustainable design with a true focus on health, wellbeing and the creation of a unique urban living environment for the City. Therefore the team must have demonstrable experience of bringing forward mixed-use schemes, in particular higher density residential, within challenging city centre environments. It is also important that the development strategy should be deliverable as well as aspirational.

description:

Support will be delivered which includes on-site carbon surveys, tailor-made carbon action plans, one-to-one support coordination, in-person and online workshops for businesses and community organisations in East Devon.\r
\r
An indicative sum of £207,000 has been allocated to this provision which includes support development costs and those associated with marketing to ensure sufficient support take up. £107,000 has been allocated for businesses and £100,000 has been allocated for community organisations.\r
\r
This programme is funded until March 2025 and so it is important that the Supplier appointed to this programme is able to mobilise quickly to ensure that support commences soon so there is as much time as possible to achieve the necessary outputs.\r
\r
The duration of this contract is for an initial 12 months with the option to extend until 31st December 2025 at the discretion of the Authority.

title: CP2524-24 ESLL Business Support
description:
The overall aim of the project is to support farm businesses in Devon to maximise their potential and productivity through regenerative and innovative methods and practices.

Agri-Advisors will be available throughout the length of the programme to ensure consistent support, in addition to specialists and consultants to explore specific topics, testing and knowledge transfer.

The role of the Agri-advisors will be to work with the Project Manager to identify key areas of demand. Provide bespoke 1-2-1 support for beneficiaries. The Agri-advisor will also be required to support farm businesses by using the Innovation Toolkit as an initial diagnostic to the business and potential areas of improvement and/or diversification. In addition to this, the Agri-advisor will need to be able to use the farm carbon toolkit to support farm businesses through an initial carbon audit. This will allow a farm business to understand their carbon footprint, potential areas of decarbonisation and sequestration. It is expected that both audits will take between 8 hours. This should leave a farm business with approximately 10 hours of free support bespoke to the needs of the farm business and their business plan (please see further details in advisor support package below). This may be required early in the programme, but it is expected that it will be available as a consistent form of support - where a farm business can call them when they need them over the length of the programme.

Followed the Restricted Procedure below threshold.
